text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
text.es: Busca las notas de la frase 1: cada una te espera hasta que estés en ella.

text.en: The Union Hymnal of 1897, the hymnal of the Central Conference of American Rabbis, prints it in four parts among its "Hebrew Hymns and Responses", with all five verses.

source.en: The Union Hymnal (Central Conference of American Rabbis, 1897), No. 17, pp. 140 and 141, read from the scan

text.en: Hear line 1, then sing it back.
Hear line 2, then sing it back.
Now lines 1 and 2 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
text.es: Ahora las frases 1 y 2 seguidas: escúchalas y repítelas.

text.en: Ein keloheinu start to end, with the guide.
Mi cheloheinu start to end, with the guide.
Node leloheinu start to end, with the guide.
Baruch eloheinu start to end, with the guide.
The whole song, with the guide.
text.es: La canción entera, con la guía.

text.en: Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
text.es: Canta tu parte con las demás voces, y la guía contigo. Mantente firme en ella mientras las otras se mueven.

text.en: The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
text.es: La guía deja de cantar: tu parte, solo con las demás voces. "Escuchar mi nota" te da tu primera nota, suave.

text.en: Once more on your own, from the top.
text.es: Otra vez sin guía, desde el principio.

text.en: Record the tune of Ein Keloheinu in Sing, with the other parts playing.
The hymnal's 1932 edition credits it to Julius Freudenthal. The 1897 edition's index gives the music's source only as "German".

source.en: The Union Hymnal (1932), No. 292, and (1897), index p. 218, read from the scans
